messages:
mike: Heads-up: CI microbench on PR #14002 failed threshold on kvcache hit-rate test after merge. p50/p95 token latency up ~12%/28% vs baseline. link: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/14002

eng-ci-bot: Benchmark run summary attached: 
- test: kvcache_hitrate_microbench
- baseline: commit f7a2d1 (2026-03-18)
- head: PR-14002
- diff: latency +28% p95, throughput -8%

tara: @mike can you paste the perf log + flamegraph? quick glance helps decide bisect vs revert :eyes:

mike: paste log snippet below:
```
KVCACHE_HIT 2026-03-19T12:01:45Z p95=48.3ms (+28%)\nBATCH_WAIT   avg=3.1ms -> 7.4ms\nKERNEL_SELECT runtime: quant_selector v2 enabled
```
flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/graphs/14002/kvcache-flame.html

sophia: hm. PR touches kernel-autoselect heuristics + batching timer tweak (reduce min-window). those two could interact: shorter batch windows -> more frequent small batches -> kvcache cold misses + more kernel switches.

dmitri: confirmed on a local repro with a small harness. profile top stacks show noisy kernel_switch at sample rate: cpu cycles spike in select_candidate(). snippet:
```
# top stacks (samples)
select_candidate()  42%\nkv_lookup()         26%\nemit_tokens()        18%\n```
I can share the harness if someone wants to run locally.

tara: ok can we bisect to the commit that introduced the batching timer change first? If that reproduces we can revert just that.

mike: PR split was: 1) kernel-autoselect tuning (commit a1b2c3), 2) batch-timer reduction (commit d4e5f6). my suspicion is d4e5f6. I'll start a bisect run on CI targeting those two commits.

eng-ci-bot: Scheduled: bisect job #bisect-14002-1 queued. Estimated runtime ~45m. Will post results.

sophia: also add a targeted unit-perf that simulates small-batch burst workload (seq-len distribution skewed to short tokens). current microbench uses uniform lengths; that may miss the regression.

dmitri: wrote a quick reproduce cmd: `scripts/bench_local --seed=burst --batch-window=2ms --kv-size=32K` reproduces 20-30% p95 spike for me. Putting it in repo/bench/ci/14002-smoke.sh

mike: nice. i'll attach that to the CI bisect so we get a focused measurement. prioritizing this since it blocks PR rollout (perf gate).

tara: thanks. if bisect returns d4e5f6 as culprit, plan is: revert d4e5f6, run full CI, then re-land kernel-autoselect tuning separately with added regression test. sound good? :+1:

eng-ci-bot: bisect job #bisect-14002-1 finished. Result: d4e5f6 (batch-timer reduction) is the likely culprit. Delta: p95 +27% when applied, baseline restored after revert. Full logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/bisect/14002/result

mike: confirmed. opened revert PR #14011 with revert of d4e5f6. posted link in the revert commit. cc @sophia @tara

sophia: great. followup: let's add the small-batch-burst test to the perf unit suite to catch this earlier. I'll file a follow-up issue to add it to goldens + run-on-merge.

mike: filing release note and marking PR-14002 blocked until revert merges. thanks everyone.
